segments: Division of responsibilities: system layer vs. user layer
System layer (NixOS): installs base packages, enables the display manager (SDDM/GDM), and loads drivers.
User layer (Home Manager): sets the wallpaper, desktop shortcuts, font sizes, and taskbar layout.
On NixOS, you do not even need to edit hyprland.conf manually.
KDE has a large and intricate set of configuration options. If you want to bring all its settings into Nix, you can use plasma-manager.
Giving GTK and Qt a consistent appearance is important.
Do not get too absorbed in configuring every pixel at this stage. Start with a usable environment, then gradually bring individual settings into Nix as you use it day to day.

Home Manager's Hyprland configuration does not replace system-level session, permission, and portal configuration. Check desktop-theme examples against your pinned Home Manager, Hyprland, and plasma-manager versions; also verify the GTK/Qt appearance in an actual session.
